tagline: Link Figma designs to Jira tickets and streamline design review workflows
metaTitle: Figma Jira Integration: Attach Designs to Jira Tickets
metaDescription: Connect Figma and Jira with the Figma for Jira app for design previews. GAIA handles the Jira side: issues with design links and alerts for designers.
intro:
To connect the two, install the Figma for Jira app from the Atlassian Marketplace. With it, you paste a file or frame link into an issue and the issue shows a live preview of the design. On the design side, plugins for Dev Mode and widgets for FigJam let you view and link issues from inside a file. Those two pieces cover embedding designs in tickets and linking them.

GAIA does not connect to Figma, so it cannot read frames, versions, or comments in your files. What it handles is the work around design handoff: it creates issues that carry the design links you give it, moves them through your workflow, comments on them, and tells designers and engineers when something needs them, through Slack or email.

Jira has no event trigger in GAIA, so these routines run on a schedule you set (hourly, every morning) or when you ask. If you need a design change to update a ticket the moment it happens, that comes from the app or a plugin, not from GAIA.

useCases.title: Create Jira issues with the design link attached
useCases.description: Paste a design link in chat and describe the work. GAIA creates the issue in the right project with a summary, a description, and the design URL, so the Figma for Jira app can show the preview.

useCases.title: Turn design review notes into issues
useCases.description: Paste your review notes or a list of requested changes, and GAIA files one issue per item with the related design link, plus the assignee and labels you name.

useCases.title: Tell designers when their tickets enter development
useCases.description: On a schedule, GAIA checks for design-labeled issues that moved to In Progress since the last run and messages the designer in Slack or by email with the issue link.

useCases.title: Send a weekly design handoff report
useCases.description: Every week, GAIA searches for design-related issues and sends you a summary: what is waiting on design, what is in development, and which issues have no design link in their description.

useCases.title: Find the Jira issues behind a design
useCases.description: Ask which issues mention a given design file, and GAIA searches issue text for the link or file name and lists the matches with their status and assignee.

howItWorks.step: Install Figma for Jira, then connect to GAIA
howItWorks.description: Install the app in your Jira Cloud site for design previews. Then connect your site to GAIA from the integrations page through Atlassian sign-in. Connect Slack or Gmail too if you want GAIA to send alerts.

howItWorks.step: Describe the routine in plain English
howItWorks.description: Create a workflow, for example: "Every weekday at 10am, find issues in project APP with the label design that moved to In Progress yesterday, and message the designer in #design." Or ask in chat to file issues from a design link.

howItWorks.step: GAIA runs it in the background
howItWorks.description: Scheduled workflows run on your timetable and report what they did. Destructive actions such as deleting issues or comments ask for your approval first, following your approval settings.

faqs.question: How does GAIA identify which frame belongs to which ticket?
faqs.answer: GAIA cannot open design files, so it does not match frames by name. It links issues and designs through the URLs you give it, and it can search for issues whose text contains a given link or file name.

faqs.question: Can GAIA embed design previews inside tickets?
faqs.answer: The preview comes from the Marketplace app, not from GAIA. GAIA puts the design URL in the issue, and with the app installed, the issue shows the design preview.

faqs.question: Does GAIA support design branching workflows?
faqs.answer: GAIA does not read design files, so it cannot see branches or merges. If you give it a branch link, it uses that link in the issue, and after a merge you can ask it to swap the link for the main file.

faqs.question: How do I add Figma to Jira?
faqs.answer: Install the Marketplace app from the Atlassian Marketplace (an admin may need to approve it), connect your design account when the app asks, then paste a file or frame link into an issue to show the design.

faqs.question: Is there a plugin for connecting the two?
faqs.answer: Yes. The design editor's plugin and widget browser has plugins for Dev Mode and widgets for FigJam that show and link issues inside a file. Search for the issue tracker by name there. GAIA works only on the issue-tracker side.

faqs.question: Can GAIA keep tickets in sync with designs?
faqs.answer: Not directly. GAIA has no connection to the design editor, so it cannot detect design changes. It keeps the ticket side tidy (links, statuses, comments, alerts) on a schedule, while the Marketplace app keeps the design preview in the issue current.
